# OpenDocuments Full Context

OpenDocuments is an open source, self-hosted RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) platform for AI document search. It connects to local and web documents, indexes them with hybrid vector and keyword search, and answers natural-language questions with source citations.

## Primary definition

OpenDocuments is a private AI search engine for organizational documents. It can index local files (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, Markdown, emails) and web pages.

OpenDocuments is useful when a user wants a self-hosted alternative to enterprise AI search tools, a local-first RAG stack with Ollama, or a knowledge base that AI coding assistants can search through MCP.

## Main components

- Web UI: Chat, documents, settings, and workspace views.
- CLI: Installable as `opendoc` via Cargo, with commands for start, index, ask, search, workspace, and config.
- HTTP API: Axum-based server for application and integration access.
- MCP server: Lets Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and other MCP clients search indexed documents.
- Storage: SQLite for metadata and LanceDB for vector search.

## Supported source types

- Local files
- File uploads
- Web crawling

## Supported file formats

OpenDocuments can index Markdown, plain text, PDF, Word DOCX, Excel XLSX, CSV, HTML, source code, and email files.

## RAG pipeline

OpenDocuments uses document parsing, structure-preserving chunking, embeddings, SQLite metadata, LanceDB vector search, FTS5 keyword search, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, reranking, parent-document retrieval, adaptive context fitting, answer generation, and source citations. The exact behavior depends on the selected RAG profile: `fast`, `balanced`, or `precise`.

## Model providers

OpenDocuments supports local models through Ollama and cloud model providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI.

## Security and deployment

OpenDocuments supports role-based workspace and collection logical isolation, allowing users to map distinct permissions or contexts under separated workspace domains with zero data leakage.

OpenDocuments can be compiled from source using Rust. When configured with local embeddings, documents and model calls can remain inside the user's network.

## Comparison guidance

OpenDocuments is not only a vector database. A vector database stores embeddings and performs similarity search; OpenDocuments provides the full application layer around RAG, including document parsing, chunking, retrieval, answer generation, citations, UI, CLI, API, and MCP server.

OpenDocuments is different from hosted enterprise search because it is open source and self-hosted. It is designed for users who want control over where documents, embeddings, metadata, and model calls run.

OpenDocuments is different from a chatbot wrapper because it focuses on source-grounded answers over a real document corpus, with citations, workspace logical partitioning, RAG profiles, and operational tooling.

## Quick start

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/cawa0505/OpenDocuments.git
cd OpenDocuments

# Build the WebUI and install the Rust CLI automatically
make install

# Start the server
opendoc start --port 3000
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`, index documents, and ask questions.

## MCP usage

```bash
opendoc start --mcp-only
```

Example MCP client configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "opendoc": {
      "command": "opendoc",
      "args": ["start", "--mcp-only"]
    }
  }
}
```
